page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What the mixture is
lines: Synthesis gas is a mixture of carbon
Small amounts of CO₂ and N₂ are also
The same mixture is called water gas, so
synthesis gas and water gas are two
steps.why: The answer to a 'what is' question is the composition. Carbon monoxide and hydrogen are the two gases that matter, and giving their rough percentages shows that neither one is a trace.
common_mistakes: Naming the mixture as CO and N₂. That composition is producer gas; synthesis gas is CO and H₂.
Writing that synthesis gas and water gas are different gases. This book and NCERT both use the two names for the same mixture.
steps.memory_tip: Synthesis gas has hydrogen in it: CO plus H₂, and the same mixture is water gas.
steps.margin_note: Name both gases and add that water gas is the other name for this mixture.

steps.label: Why it is called synthesis gas

lines.text: Synthesis gas is used to make methanol

lines: The mixture is the starting material for
Because it is used to synthesise these
compounds, it is named synthesis gas,
shortened in industry to syn gas.
steps.why: The name is not arbitrary, and saying where it comes from is what turns a memorised composition into an answer. The mixture is fed to industrial plants that build larger molecules from it, so it is the gas used for synthesis.
common_mistakes: Writing that it is called synthesis gas because it is synthesised. It is named for what is made FROM it, such as methanol.
Giving only the composition. One closing line naming what the gas is used to make completes the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Synthesis gas is the gas that synthesises other things — methanol first of all.
steps.margin_note: Naming one product such as methanol is what shows the reason for the name.

insider_note: Water gas and synthesis gas are two names for one mixture. What this question asks for is the composition and the reason for the name, not the preparation.
